content.text:
I reviewed the brief line by line against the 8-K Exhibit 99.1.

**Key findings:**
- Facts f05 (ROTCE 29% / 23% ex-items) and f06 (NII $25.6B, up 10%) are missing entirely from the brief — notable omissions given ROTCE is headlined in the release and quoted by Dimon.
- The AWM line contains two problems: revenue growth is given as 18% (that is the AUM growth rate; AWM net revenue rose 19%), and the "nearly 44,000 first-time investors" record is pulled from Dimon's CCB/wealth management commentary, not AWM.
- The watch-item framing that the firm has "exposure to large global fiscal deficits" is the analyst's inference; Dimon lists fiscal deficits as a macro risk, not a firm exposure.
- Figures for net income, EPS, ex-items results, revenue (both bases correctly labeled), expense, overhead ratio, credit costs, CET1, TLAC, book values and distributions all tie to the release.

facts.evidence: Reported revenue reached $57.3 billion, while managed revenue totaled $58.0 billion, with expenses at $27.3 billion resulting in a reported overhead ratio of 48%.
The Firm reported second-quarter 2026 net income of $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share, representing a 41% increase compared to the prior-year quarter.
Net income excluding significant items was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share, reflecting a 13% increase year over year.
Commercial & Investment Banking (CIB) revenue grew 27% year over year to $24.9 billion, propelled by a 30% increase in Investment Banking fees and a 35% rise in Markets revenue.
the $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares and $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments which collectively reduced adjusted net income by $4.2 billion after tax
Capital distributions included a common dividend of $4.0 billion and $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases, resulting in a net payout of 73% for the last twelve months.
CET1 Capital Ratios were 14.1% under the Standardized approach and 14.2% under the Advanced approach, with Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity at $590 billion.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion, comprising $2.4 billion of net charge-offs and a $149 million net reserve build.

claims.claim: Second-quarter 2026 net income was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share.
Net income rose 41% versus the prior-year quarter.
Net income excluding significant items was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share.
Net income excluding significant items increased 13% year over year.
Reported revenue was $57.3 billion.
Managed revenue was $58.0 billion.
Expense was $27.3 billion.
The reported overhead ratio was 48%.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion.
Net charge-offs were $2.4 billion.
There was a $149 million net reserve build.
CIB revenue grew 27% year over year to $24.9 billion.
CIB growth was propelled by a 30% increase in Investment Banking fees.
CIB growth was propelled by a 35% rise in Markets revenue.
CCB net income increased 3% to $5.3 billion.
CCB revenue grew 8%.
The Card Services net charge-off rate was 3.34%.
AWM generated $6.9 billion in revenue.
AWM revenue increased 18% year over year.
claims.note: Release states AWM net revenue of $6.9 billion was up 19%; 18% is the growth rate of AUM, not revenue.

claims.claim: AWM assets under management reached $5.1 trillion.
AWM revenue growth was driven by first-time investors hitting a record of nearly 44,000.
claims.note: The nearly 44,000 record first-time investors is cited by Dimon under CCB wealth management, not AWM, and is not given as a driver of AWM revenue (release cites management fees, net inflows, valuation gains, loans and brokerage).

claims.claim: Jamie Dimon is Chairman and said the U.S. economy has shown resiliency supported by AI-driven capital investment and fiscal stimulus.
Dimon said several risks are shifting below the surface, including geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation, large global fiscal deficits and elevated asset prices.
Management stated it cannot predict how these forces will ultimately play out and emphasized careful monitoring of risks to prepare for a wide range of scenarios.
The release contains no specific numerical guidance or outlook for future quarters.
The firm states that actual results may differ materially from forward-looking statements, which are subject to significant risks and uncertainties.
The CET1 capital ratio was 14.1% under the Standardized approach and 14.2% under the Advanced approach.
Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity was $590 billion.
Book value per share increased 9% year over year to $133.01.
Tangible book value per share rose 10% to $113.35.
Capital distributions included a common dividend of $4.0 billion.
Capital distributions included $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases.
Net payout for the last twelve months was 73%.
Significant items were a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares and $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments.
These significant items collectively account for a $4.2 billion after-tax difference between reported and ex-items net income.
The firm has exposure to large global fiscal deficits.
claims.note: Dimon lists large global fiscal deficits as a macro risk shifting below the surface; the release makes no statement about firm exposure to them.
